close_reason: Changed MdnSendResponse.not_sent from Option<HashMap<String, Value>> to Option<HashMap<String, SetError>>. Matches the workspace canonical pattern jmap-types::SetResponse.not_created: HashMap<String, SetError>. The doc comment's 'upward dependency on the server crate' claim was wrong — SetError lives in jmap-types, which jmap-mail-types already depends on. Wire-byte-identical (SetError is a plain derive-Serialize struct). Updated the response rustdoc. cargo test clean — the server-side response building already produces wire JSON via json!() macro, not via MdnSendResponse struct serialization, so server code unchanged. description:
## Caller contract risk: response error map is untyped where the workspace's canonical pattern is typed.

\`MdnSendResponse.not_sent\` is declared:

```rust
pub not_sent: Option<HashMap<String, Value>>,
```

with a doc comment stating \"values are JMAP SetError objects (RFC 8620 §5.3) serialized as JSON objects; they are typed as Value here to avoid an upward dependency on the server crate.\"

The \"upward dependency\" comment is incorrect. \`SetError\` is defined in \`jmap-types\` (\`crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:162\`), the foundation crate that \`jmap-mail-types\` already depends on. The canonical workspace pattern for the same field shape is in \`SetResponse\` (\`crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:282-286\`):

```rust
pub not_created: Option<HashMap<String, SetError>>,
pub not_updated: Option<HashMap<Id, SetError>>,
pub not_destroyed: Option<HashMap<Id, SetError>>,
```

i.e. the foundation crate keys creation-id error maps by \`String\` and types the values as \`SetError\`. The same shape on \`MdnSendResponse.not_sent\` would be wire-byte-identical and would not introduce any new dependency.

### What callers cannot rely on today

A client that receives an \`MDN/send\` response and wants to render the per-creation-id errors must call \`serde_json::from_value::<SetError>(value)\` on each entry by hand. Nothing in the type tells them this is required; nothing in the type stops a buggy server from returning a non-SetError shape that the client will then accept silently.

### Same diff, inconsistent fix

The same diff converted \`MdnSendRequest.on_success_update_email: Option<HashMap<String, Value>>\` to \`Option<HashMap<Id, PatchObject>>\` — wire-identical due to \`#[serde(transparent)]\`, but typed-up. The parallel server-side error map was left as \`Value\`. The two changes have the same shape and the same justification; only one was made.

### Recommended fix

```rust
pub not_sent: Option<HashMap<String, SetError>>,
```

This is wire-byte-identical (SetError is just a derive-Serialize struct), strictly more type-safe, and matches the workspace canonical \`SetResponse.not_created\` pattern verbatim.

### Cross-references

- \`crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs:282-286\` — workspace canonical SetResponse error-map pattern.
- bd JMAP-zx3s diff: \`crate-jmap-mail-types/src/mdn.rs:277\` (unchanged in this diff but in the same file as the partial fix).
title: MdnSendResponse.not_sent: Option<HashMap<String, Value>> — Value erases SetError typing already available in jmap-types
